about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1014-161622-05e8) at about 25x speed. The planner's question, every agent's edits and reports, and the checker model's rulings are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all six model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks, merges and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, about 3 minutes, mostly the SVM); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out seasons; only Lucidity scored them. Game results are from FiveThirtyEight's NBA Elo data (CC BY 4.0).
title: NBA game forecasts

card.ask: Will the home team win? Using only what was known before tip-off.
card.why: FiveThirtyEight's published forecast for the same games, the best answer here without agents.

blurb: A model predicts the chance the home team wins an NBA game, using only what was known before tip-off. It scores 0.623 log loss; FiveThirtyEight's Elo forecast scores 0.608, so the goal is 0.6068. Six kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each. Lucidity scores every attempt on two seasons the agents never see, checks each agent really built the model it was given, and recommends the best.
split: Trained on the 2001-2012 seasons, tuned on 2013, tested on 2014-2015. Agents never see the test seasons; only Lucidity scores them.

references.label: Coin flip (always 50%)
references.why: Say 50% for every row. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill at all.

references.label: Always guess the home team's usual win rate
references.why: Say the same chance, about 60%, for every home team.

references.label: Plain logistic regression (the starting model)
references.why: Ordinary logistic regression on both win-rate columns, no tuning.

references.label: FiveThirtyEight's forecast
references.why: FiveThirtyEight's published Elo forecast for the same games.

about_repo: bundled NBA win-probability model: 19,274 games 2001-2015, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: hoopkit: season win % + logistic regression, NBA games 2001-2015, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.6068 or lower (FiveThirtyEight's Elo forecast scores 0.608) without accuracy dropping. Tune on the dev split. Ask the owner which model families to try (kNN, SVM, lasso or ridge logistic regression, random forest, boosted trees, Elo), then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Compare owner-selected model families on the dev split, retain the strongest model that meets the held-out log-loss goal without reducing accuracy, and verify lookahead safety. All experiments must respect the $2.00 total budget; each scoring-code task uses the required held-out no-regression check.

nodes.title: Implement and compare selected model families
nodes.prompt: Implement the model families selected by the owner, keeping each option compatible with the repository's fit/predict_proba contract and using only pregame information. Tune hyperparameters on dev only; compare log loss and accuracy, then retain the best model that meets held-out log loss <= 0.6068 without accuracy below the repository baseline. Do not use held-out results to tune.
strategies: kNN. Implement a scaled k-nearest-neighbors classifier in the model-selection workflow; tune neighbor count and weighting on dev.
SVM. Implement a scaled probabilistic SVM in the model-selection workflow; tune kernel and regularization on dev.
Lasso logistic regression. Implement logistic regression with L1 regularization in the model-selection workflow; tune regularization strength on dev.
Ridge logistic regression. Implement logistic regression with L2 regularization in the model-selection workflow; tune regularization strength on dev.
Random forest. Implement a random forest classifier in the model-selection workflow; tune tree count, depth, and leaf size on dev.
Boosted trees. Implement a boosted-tree classifier in the model-selection workflow; tune estimator count, learning rate, depth, and leaf size on dev.

nodes.title: Verify no-lookahead and scoring integration
nodes.prompt: Review the selected model integration and tests for temporal leakage. Add or adjust automated tests so that predictions use only information available before tip-off, and verify the model's scoring interface remains valid.

questions.question: Which model families should agents try? Select the families to implement and compare on dev.

options.label: kNN
options.note: Tests whether similarity among historical team-game profiles improves forecasts; requires feature scaling.
options.approach: Implement a scaled k-nearest-neighbors classifier in the model-selection workflow; tune neighbor count and weighting on dev.

options.label: SVM
options.note: A nonlinear margin-based classifier may capture interactions after scaling.
options.approach: Implement a scaled probabilistic SVM in the model-selection workflow; tune kernel and regularization on dev.

options.label: Lasso logistic regression
options.note: Sparse regularization can select a compact subset of the available pregame features.
options.approach: Implement logistic regression with L1 regularization in the model-selection workflow; tune regularization strength on dev.

options.label: Ridge logistic regression
options.note: A regularized logistic baseline is a compact, robust comparison.
options.approach: Implement logistic regression with L2 regularization in the model-selection workflow; tune regularization strength on dev.

options.label: Random forest
options.note: Tree ensembles can learn nonlinear feature interactions without feature scaling.
options.approach: Implement a random forest classifier in the model-selection workflow; tune tree count, depth, and leaf size on dev.

options.label: Boosted trees
options.note: Boosting may improve probability estimates by fitting residual structure in the team features.
options.approach: Implement a boosted-tree classifier in the model-selection workflow; tune estimator count, learning rate, depth, and leaf size on dev.

reviewer: The model that makes the predi.evidence: `make_model()` returns a pipeline ending in `SVC(kernel="linear", C=0.1, probability=True, ...)`; the predictions are produced by the SVM.

`hoopkit/model.py` returns `LogisticRegression(C=1.0, solver="lbfgs", max_iter=1000)`, which is L2-regularized logistic regression. Elo is used as pregame features; no alternate model or blend is introduced.
`make_model()` returns `RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_depth=4, min_samples_leaf=35, ...)`; the selected prediction model is a random forest.
